The rule is: For each column containing the minority color, (1) convert all majority colors above any minority color position to the minority color, (2) convert majority colors below minorities to minority color except for the bottom-most majority position which becomes black (0). In the test grid, magenta (6) is the minority color with 3 instances, and gray (5) is the majority color with 15 instances. Applying the rule: Column 0 has minority at row 5, so gray at row 4 becomes magenta, and gray at row 8 becomes black. Column 3 has minority at row 2, so grays at rows 0,1 become magenta, and grays below (rows 3,4,5,6) stay gray except the bottom-most which would become black, but there are multiple non-contiguous grays so the last gray in this column becomes black. Column 6 has minority at row 5, so grays above (row 3,4) become magenta, and grays below (rows 6,7,8) become magenta except the last one becomes black.

Rule: For each column containing the minority color (less frequent non-black color): convert all majority colors above each minority position to minority color, and convert the bottom-most majority color in that column to black (0). Majority colors between or below minorities become minority color except for the very last one which becomes black.
